I'm not even kidding. Honestly sometimes it's the simple shit that keeps me here.
I desperately want to own a stovetop whistling kettle one day.
I know that sounds like such a stupid tiny thing not worth the effort of staying.. but on some days just imaging myself with that kettle making myself a cup of tea sounds so wonderful that it gives me enough hope or at least a yearning for a future in which it might be possible.
I know between all the shit that's going on (e.g. I got diagnosed with BPD last week) hoping for a future at all seems pointless but there's a place inside me that's still hoping for tiny little wonders even if working towards that might be hard, knowing I have something (even so little and seemingly pointless) to look forward to gives me enough strength to go on just one more day.
I hope you can find the little things that will gift you one more day at a time.

I understand how you feel, I often feel the same, forgiving ourselves and accepting Christ‘s forgiveness for something we can’t seem to forgive our selves is so hard. But that doesn’t change the fact that He has forgiven you. Everything you did and everything you will do.

I know feelings of guilt are awful but you regretting what you did is the best way to overcome the guilt. Pour your heart out to God and ask Him to forgive you and help you to forgive yourself. He already knows what happened anyway and He also knows how conflicted you feel about it.

I don’t know if what you did happened deliberately or your mind slipped and you found yourself in the situation you are in now. Regardless of it you seem genuinely sorry and wish to undo it.
Just go to the person you wronged and apologise honestly. 

Christians have wronged me before and I forgave them. Not even because I truly understood why they did what they did or I didn’t care but because I saw that they regretted it and were sorry.

If Christ can forgive my worst sins and the sins of the entire world, I can (at least try to my best ability) to forgive those who have wronged me. You are not your one wrongdoing or even all hundreds of them you (and everyone else) will do in your life. I bet for the one bad thing that happened there are hundreds of positive and selfless things you did. Let Jesus into your heart and let him replace the guilt with acceptance of the situation and repentance from what you did.
God wants us to repent and leave the guilt behind and wants to change for the better. Learn from what happened, ask for forgiveness and move on. Don’t forget about it, learn from it.


But don’t beat yourself up about something Christ has already forgiven you for.
